Email meSee my aircraft

Build it. Fly it. Break it. Understand it. Make it better.

I love taking a complicated system (motors, sensors, flight controllers, computers, software, structures) and making all of those pieces behave as one.

I started by building things: a CNC machine, robotic arms, and a lot of electronics. That curiosity grew into designing and flying increasingly complex UAVs, from a heavy-lift autonomous multirotor to a hybrid VTOL aircraft that transitions between hover and efficient forward flight.

Now at Johns Hopkins, I'm studying robotics with a focus on automation and control. My interest has moved beyond building robots to making autonomous systems reliable.

I've worked on hardware-in-the-loop testing, avionics fault injection, flight-test systems, sensor integration, telemetry, autonomous navigation, computer vision, and hardware/software debugging. At Joby Aviation I built a fault-injection PCB for avionics verification.

What I enjoy most is finding the failure at the boundary between hardware and software, building a way to reproduce it, and designing a better system. Aerospace is unforgiving: a system can't just work in a demo. It has to work repeatedly, under uncertainty, in the real world.

Systems Integration

I learned integration by leading it. As Chief Technical Officer and then President of UAS@UCLA, I oversaw airframe manufacturing, electronics integration, and flight testing across three aircraft, working with the flight controls and propulsion teams to tune PID loops and validate performance in the field.

Aetherguard: Indoor Patrol Drone

UCLA degree capstone, 2026

An autonomous indoor security and patrol drone for warehouses and homes. It combines onboard vision, LiDAR, and real-time decision-making for obstacle avoidance and human recognition.

  • Nvidia Jetson Orin Nano companion computer paired with a Pixhawk 6C flight controller
  • MAVLink, optical flow, and 360° LiDAR for localization in GPS-denied spaces
  • Facial recognition and alert logic in Python and OpenCV
JetsonPixhawk 6CMAVLinkLiDAROpenCV

Autonomous eVTOL

UAS@UCLA R&D, 2025. I led this as club President.

A hybrid aircraft that takes off vertically and cruises efficiently on its wing for long-range autonomous missions. 2 m wingspan, 22 minutes of cruise endurance.

  • Quad-plus-dual tilt-motor layout for a smooth hover-to-cruise transition
  • Pixhawk 6X with ArduPilot for flight control, telemetry, and mission planning
  • Modified Anaconda RC airframe reinforced with composites
Pixhawk 6XArduPilotPID tuningComposites

Spinny: Heavy-Lift Autonomous Drone

UAS@UCLA, 2024. I was Chief Technical Officer.

A 6.5 ft wingspan modular test platform for guidance and perception systems. It carries up to 25 lb with RTK GPS precision.

  • Cube Orange+, RTK GPS, IR height sensor, and Raspberry Pi camera
  • Redundant communication, power isolation, and real-time data logging
  • Autonomous navigation validated through multiple field tests

Multi-UAV Swarm Research

Ascend swarm drones, ongoing

Investigating cooperative reconnaissance: centralized and decentralized coordination, coverage planning that minimizes overlap, and inter-UAV communication, built on ROS 2 and PX4.

Testing

My testing experience comes from Joby Aviation, where I coordinated with cross-functional engineers and technicians to design, assemble, and run test rigs for vehicle subsystems, and ran HIL procedures in National Instruments LabVIEW on the ITL to support live flight operations in Dubai.

Avionics Fault-Injection PCB

Joby Aviation, 2025

A custom hardware-in-the-loop board that simulates transient faults and signal interruptions under controlled conditions. I built it under a tight deadline. It was validated on the first iteration and scaled to a bulk order for multiple lab facilities.

  • Designed and assembled in Altium Designer
  • High-frequency relay switching for precise transient faults
  • Impedance-matched differential pairs for ARINC-compliant signal integrity
  • LEMO connectors for rugged, low-noise aircraft-grade interfacing
AltiumHILARINCLabVIEW

Electric Motor Thrust Test Stand

Propulsion characterization

A CAD-designed stand built from aluminum extrusion that measures thrust, electrical and mechanical power, motor and ESC efficiency, and propeller efficiency across the RPM range. I use the data to choose motor and propeller pairs.

Flight and Field Testing

UAS@UCLA and Matter Intelligence

Repeated field tests to validate navigation and sensors, plus flying data-collection missions with LiDAR and imagery, and analyzing telemetry afterward.

Design & Manufacturing

I started designing in high school and kept going. I now work in SolidWorks, 3DX CATIA, Fusion 360, and Altium, and as a UCLA Makerspace Technician I ran 3D printers and CNC machines and helped students manufacture their own parts.

Compact CNC Mill

Geitonas School, 2022

A low-cost milling machine for makerspaces, modeled in Fusion 360 with 3D-printed and aluminum structure. It runs open-source GRBL on a Makerbase MKS DLC board, with limit switches, emergency stop, and modular toolheads.

6-DOF Educational Robot Arm

Nokia, 2022

Inspired by the Niryo One, with 440 mm reach and a 400 g payload. A Raspberry Pi 3 B+ and TinyG controller drive four steppers and two servos, with swappable end effectors and a Python/ROS interface that K-12 students can program.

VL53L9CX LiDAR Evaluation Board

Altium Designer

A custom PCB for ST's time-of-flight sensor, from schematic with level shifting and regulators through layout and 3D review.
